dynamic_tariff_scheduling_tip: The electricity price we obtain from EPEX or other public channels is the <highlight>market price</highlight>, which is the transaction price of electricity in the market and usually changes with demand and supply. However, please note that the price on your electricity bill is usually the <highlight>settlement price</highlight>, which includes additional fees such as transportation fees, distribution fees, and taxes and may be significantly different from the market price. Therefore, when you optimize the charging and discharging time of energy storage system in AlphaESS based on the dynamic market price, we recommend that you take this difference into account and check the actual settlement price with your electricity supplier. This helps you make the optimal energy storage decision.
expected_return_usd_tips_1: Under full charge and discharge conditions, Expected Profit = Selling Price × Discharged Energy – Buying Price × Charged Energy.
expected_return_usd_tips_2: The expected profit is for reference only, to assist the user in setting high and low electricity price range, and serves no other purpose.
high_electricity_prices_tip: The data corresponding to the time point in this period is the high electricity price, and the proportion of the total data packets in the period of high electricity price every day. The data packets obtained by the system from the electricity price market are sorted from low to high every day, such as setting the high electricity price range to 70%, calculating 24 packets of data * 70% of the time for high electricity prices, the system rounds the calculation results and marks them with red lines, and after obtaining the electricity price for a new day every day, it will recalculate the threshold range of high electricity prices.
high_less_price_range_tips: The high electricity price range must be at least 5% higher than the low electricity price range
low_electricity_prices_tip: The data corresponding to the time point in this period is low electricity price, and the proportion of the total data packets during the period of low electricity price every day. The system obtains data packages from the electricity price market every day in order from low to high, such as setting the low electricity price range to 30%, calculating 24 packets of data * 30% of the time for low electricity price, the system rounds the calculation results and marks them with green lines, and after obtaining the electricity price for a new day every day, the threshold range of low electricity prices will be recalculated.
neg_electricity_price_dispatch_tip: To comply with the provisions effective from March 2025 in Germany, the Energy Industry Act (EnWG) Amendment 2025, AlphaESS integrates historical solar data, weather forecasts, and other relevant information to intelligently predict power generation during periods of negative electricity tariffs. Before the anticipated negative tariff periods, the system will automatically adjust the battery charging and discharging strategy, releasing some stored energy in advance to reduce the risk of feeding energy into the grid. Please note that the forecast data is for reference only, and actual power generation may deviate due to weather, device status, and other factors, which could still result in grid feed-in during negative tariff periods. We recommend that users monitor system data in real time and decide whether to enable this feature based on their actual usage to achieve more efficient energy management. Please note that this regulation only applies to users from March 2025 onwards. Before enabling this feature, please confirm that you are within the applicable scope. When enabled, this feature's energy scheduling strategy will take precedence over the custom scheduling strategy based on dynamic tariffs.
price_range_notifications: High and low electricity price intervals are notified, while regular electricity price intervals are not notified.
